eyebrow: Snowflake Data Engineering Capstone · Ch.2, L.8
subtitle: The actual MRR and churn measures leadership asked for

code:
MRR =
CALCULATE(
  SUM(fct_subscriptions[amount_usd]),
  fct_subscriptions[event_type] IN {"signup","upgrade"},
  dim_subscribers[cancelled_at] = BLANK()
)
caption: A plain SUM would wrongly include cancellation events and past, inactive subscribers.

eyebrow: The measure lands on a Card visual
caption: A real Power BI Desktop Card-building flow -- Driftwood's MRR, churn-rate, and subscriber-count tiles are built this same way.

eyebrow: Churn rate: a ratio, not a count
code:
Subscribers Cancelled This Month = CALCULATE(
  DISTINCTCOUNT(dim_subscribers[subscriber_id]),
  dim_subscribers[cancelled_at] >= STARTOFMONTH(TODAY())
)

Churn Rate = DIVIDE(
  [Subscribers Cancelled This Month],
  [Active Subscribers Start of Month]
)
caption: DIVIDE returns BLANK(), not an error, the first month with no baseline yet.

caption: A real Power BI Desktop Add Visual flow -- the same workflow used for every tile on this dashboard.
